proposals.before: For the Huiyuan calendar, from the Superior Origin in the year jiazi to the third year of Shaoxi (1190), year xinhai, the accumulated count is 25,494,767 years.
proposals.after: For the Huiyuan calendar, from the Superior Origin in the year jiazi to the third year of Shaoxi (1192), year xinhai, the accumulated count is 25,494,767 years.
proposals.reason: Shaoxi 3 corresponds to AD 1192, not 1190 (Shaoxi 1). The parenthetical Western year is wrong.
Chinese 二百三十二萬二千 is 2,322,000; the English adds an erroneous extra 200.

proposals.before: Huiyuan: two million three hundred twenty-two thousand two hundred.
proposals.after: Huiyuan: two million three hundred twenty-two thousand.
proposals.reason: Chinese 二百三十二萬二千 is 2,322,000; the literal invents “two hundred.”
In calendrical fractions 少 means one quarter, not seven-eighths.

proposals.before: Dusk-and-dawn remainder count: one hundred seventy-three and slightly less.
proposals.after: Dusk-and-dawn remainder count: one hundred seventy-three and a quarter.
proposals.reason: 少 is the calendrical quarter fraction, not “slightly less.”

decisions.reason: Chinese 紹熙三年 is Shaoxi year 3 (AD 1192); the parenthetical (1190) is Shaoxi 1 and must be corrected to 1192.
二百三十二萬二千 is 2,322,000 (232×10,000 + 2,000); 2,322,200 invents an extra 200 absent from the Chinese.
二百三十二萬二千 reads “two million three hundred twenty-two thousand”; the literal’s “two hundred” is not in the Chinese.
In calendrical remainder notation 少 is the quarter fraction (¼), not seven-eighths; 一百七十三少 is therefore 173¼.
少 after an integer remainder is the calendrical quarter, not “slightly less”; the literal should be “one hundred seventy-three and a quarter.”
